bullets.title: FOMC Day: Warsh's first meeting; market pricing hold with easing bias likely removed
bullets.body: The market's central focus today is Warsh's debut FOMC press conference. Consensus expects rates held unchanged, with the median dot plot likely dropping any 2026 cut signal — UBS sees no cuts until 2028. Key debate is whether Warsh signals dovish optionality or a hawkish lean; options imply +/-74bps SPX move on the day. Markets currently price ~0.85 Fed hikes by year-end.

bullets.title: Fed reaction function: core inflation overshoot seen temporary; 30-40% odds of hike cycle if PCE stays elevated
bullets.body: Investors now broadly expect no cuts or hikes for remainder of 2026, with the Fed expected to look through tariff/war-driven inflation. Core inflation overshoot is viewed as supply-driven, not labor-driven; Atlanta Fed wage growth at 3.5% with ~2% productivity implies Core PCE drifting to 1.5-2% longer term. However, 30-40% odds of a 2-4 hike cycle exist if core CPI doesn't slow to 3.3% or lower — 48% of investors now believe core CPI is on a Fed-friendly glide path, up from 35% at month start.

bullets.title: US-Iran MOU triggers oil supply normalization; WTI near Citi's bearish $75 Q3 target
bullets.body: A US-Iran framework MOU — including $300B economic package, oil sanctions relief, and Strait of Hormuz reopening — has shifted oil markets from war-risk pricing to implementation-risk pricing. WTI fell ~$15/bbl over four sessions to ~$75.77, approaching Citi's bearish Q3 $75 and Q4 $70 forecasts; CTAs reportedly triggering shorts at $75. IEA cut 2026 global oil demand forecast by 700K bpd and warned of a significant 2027 glut (8.0M bpd supply growth vs 2.0M bpd demand growth).

bullets.title: JPM flips tactically bullish; raises AI capex forecast to $5.5T through 2030
bullets.body: JPM shifted to Tactically Bullish from cautious, citing the Iran deal as catalyst for a broad risk-on impulse. Separately, JPM raised total AI capex estimates to $5.5T through 2030 (from $5.1T), with $4.1T in debt financing and 138 GW data center capacity base case. MSFT flagged as ~1 year behind on funding curve with a $90-130B gap in FY27-28, likely the largest new IG supply source in 2H26. Data center financing has already reached $58B YTD vs. $34B year-prior, up 71%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor upcycle intact: April sales beat seasonality; DRAM ASPs +18.5% M/M, NAND +33% M/M
bullets.body: April semiconductor sales declined only 2.3% M/M vs. the typical ~11% seasonal trend, with overall ASPs flat vs. the usual 2-3% decline. DRAM ASPs surged 18.5% M/M and NAND 33% M/M on tight supply; total semis revenue rose 115% Y/Y — the 31st consecutive month of Y/Y growth. UBS forecasts the global semis 3MMA growth rate peaks at +135% Y/Y in October 2026, with preferred names MU and NVDA.

bullets.title: Citi raises MU PT to $1,200; DRAM ASPs forecast +200% in 2026, undersupply through 2027
bullets.body: Citi raised MU FY26/27 EPS by 4-10% and lifted the price target to $1,200 (10x CY27 EPS) on better-than-expected memory pricing. DRAM spot prices are up 52% since January and 22% since April, trading 21% above contract pricing; Citi projects full-year 2026 DRAM ASP growth of +200% and NAND ASPs +186%. Global DRAM is expected to remain 5% undersupplied in 2026, with the upcycle extending through 2027.

bullets.title: Citi raises WFE targets: AMAT to $710, LRCX to $450, KLAC to $290; sees $250B WFE by 2028
bullets.body: Citi updated its WFE bull case to $145B/$200B/$250B in CY26/27/28, driven by AI-driven agentic workloads expanding KV cache footprints and NAND demand. Nvidia reduced HBM2 DRAM in Vera Rubin NVL72 systems by ~50% due to supply constraints, creating structural pressure requiring 2-4 new NAND greenfield fabs ($15-30B NAND WFE). AMAT PT raised to $710, LRCX to $450, KLAC to $290 on CY28 earnings power.

bullets.title: Hedge fund net exposure at 4-year highs; Semis net allocation doubled YTD; Mag 7 at 1-year net exposure low
bullets.body: Goldman Prime reports global Fundamental L/S funds up +15.4% YTD with +8.4% alpha; net exposure rose +6.2 pts to 4-year highs (89th percentile). Net allocation to Semis & Semi Equipment more than doubled YTD to record highs driven by Asia chip maker buying. Conversely, Mag 7 net exposure fell to 1-year lows with record short selling, despite US Info Tech exposures at 5-year highs — a divergence suggesting rotation within tech rather than out of it.

bullets.title: $7.5T options expiry on June 18: largest on record, potential for select-name volatility
bullets.body: Citi flags $7.5T notional open interest expiring June 18 — the largest in recent history vs. the prior $7T December 2025 record. The expiry represents 9.9% of Russell 3000 market cap, with single-stock options notional volume up 24% in June vs. YTD average. While intra-day volatility on triple-witching days is historically in-line or lower than other expiries, 50 options chains have been identified with strikes within +/-2% of current price and significant open interest relative to trading volume.

bullets.title: JBL beats across the board; raises FY guidance — AI infrastructure demand 'extremely strong'
bullets.body: Jabil reported FQ3 revenue of $8.8B (vs. Street $8.64B) and EPS of $3.16 (vs. $3.10), with Intelligent Infrastructure segment +21% YoY. FQ4 guidance of $9.6B revenue midpoint and $4.00 EPS midpoint both meaningfully above Street ($8.96B/$3.72). Full-year FY26 revenue guidance raised to $35B from $34B; management described AI infrastructure demand as 'extremely strong' with higher full-year AI-related revenue outlook.

bullets.title: INTC 18A-P enters risk production — potential Apple foundry deal back in focus
bullets.body: Intel began risk production of its advanced 18A-P chip node at the VLSI Symposium, meeting initial timeline expectations and unlocking external customer manufacturing capability. Multiple sources note this revives speculation around an Apple foundry deal. HP is also separately shifting CPU demand to AMD and Qualcomm due to Intel's lower availability as Intel focuses on Panther Lake; supply constraints at Intel are expected through 2027E per Mizuho.

bullets.title: AVGO targeting $250-300B FY28 XPU revenue; Apollo/Blackstone financing could triple Anthropic/OpenAI volumes
bullets.body: AVGO's XPV financing structure — with Apollo/Blackstone — would fund Anthropic FY26 purchases in the first tranche, and if fully executed, allow Anthropic/OpenAI XPU volumes to triple to 15GW in FY28. AVGO is targeting $250-300B in FY28 XPU revenue at $10-15B content per GW, with AVGO providing residual value guarantees as backstop. JPM separately flagged AVGO/Apollo/Blackstone AI XPV JV ($30B) as a paradigm for public market AI financing.

bullets.title: Inference-as-a-Service demand to outstrip supply through 2027; agentic workloads consuming 23x more tokens
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag that agentic AI workloads consume 23x more tokens than conversational tasks, driving a Jevons dynamic where efficiency gains are being fully re-absorbed. Inference-as-a-Service demand is expected to exceed supply through 2027, with workload-to-chip matching becoming the key vendor differentiator. Data center financing has surged to $58B YTD (vs. $34B prior year), with European capacity projected to grow from 8GW to 41GW by 2035.

bullets.title: Microsoft shifts Copilot to multi-model architecture with Anthropic and DeepSeek for cost control
bullets.body: Microsoft is transitioning Copilot from an OpenAI-exclusive model to a multi-model orchestration approach incorporating Anthropic's Claude and evaluating DeepSeek for low-cost inference, driven by usage-based pricing economics that require controlling inference costs. Separately, MSFT and Oracle's $3B cloud infrastructure deal collapsed. Enterprise AI cost resistance has risen materially, driving a shift to cheaper/open-source models — viewed as a speed bump, not a secular slowdown.

bullets.title: White House weighing government equity stakes in AI companies; Anthropic model release restricted
bullets.body: Trump administration officials are actively discussing structures for potential government equity stakes in major AI labs, while the White House separately restricted Anthropic's Fable model release last week. Lutnick warned that Anthropic needs government approval before granting foreigners access to AI models, accelerating congressional AI guardrail momentum. The US and Europe are also discussing a scheme to allow close allies access to the latest AI models.

bullets.title: Sector rotation broadening: Healthcare, Reshoring, and Short-Cycle Industrials rising; AI trade crowding
bullets.body: UBS's Theme-ometer shows Healthcare globally at the top of preferred themes for the first time in months, alongside US Reshoring and Short Cycle Industrials moving into clearly positive territory. AI Winners and AI-exposed Semis remain supported but face crowding and valuation headwinds. Consumer cyclicals and staples remain weakest on negative earnings revisions. US single stock flows show broadening with 8 of 11 sectors net bought MTD, led by Financials, Industrials, and Consumer Discretionary.

bullets.title: UK CPI misses at 2.8% (vs 3.3% BoE forecast); reduces urgency for further tightening
bullets.body: UK May CPI held at 2.8% YoY, a second consecutive downside surprise vs. the BoE's 3.3% forecast; core CPI came in at 2.6% vs. the 2.8% forecast. JPM revised its UK CPI peak forecast down from 3.8% to 3.4% in November. The BoE is likely to maintain a tightening bias in tomorrow's communications but with reduced urgency; the July hike odds have diminished, with the voting forecast remaining 7-2 for hold.

bullets.title: OpenAI burned $3.7B in Q1 2026 on $5.7B revenue; gross margins improved to ~39%
bullets.body: OpenAI burned $3.7B in Q1 2026, representing over half of its $5.7B quarterly revenue, ending the quarter with $73B in cash. Gross margins improved to ~39% from 33% in the prior year, suggesting improving unit economics even as absolute losses remain enormous. The figures highlight the scale of capital required to sustain frontier AI model development.

bullets.title: China macro deteriorating: May retail sales -0.6% YoY, first decline since Dec-22; MSCI China near bear market
bullets.body: China May 2026 retail sales declined 0.6% YoY — the first drop since December 2022, missing consensus of -0.2% — with autos, home appliances, and home furnishings each down 14-16% YoY. MSCI China is down ~18% from its October peak, approaching bear market territory, as AI investors shift focus to hard-tech semis (Korea MSCI +125% YTD, Taiwan +63% YTD) away from consumer-facing Hong Kong platforms. FDI has slowed to a standstill and broker estimates for HK tech are being cut ~3% Y/Y.

bullets.title: Quadruple witching + FOMC = elevated near-term vol risk; medium-term momentum at 98th percentile crowding
bullets.body: The combination of $7.5T options expiry on June 18 and FOMC uncertainty creates a near-term volatility setup. Separately, Medium-Term Momentum factor exposure is near record highs at the 98th percentile and Long/Short Crowdedness is approaching 5-year extremes — a fragile positioning backdrop. Hedgeye flags QQQ forming its first lower-high in risk range, with immediate S&P 500 range at 7,256-7,625 and UST 10yr yield range 4.38-4.56%.
